Claude & privacy Invited beta

Analysis with Anthropic Claude

Operational TraceRook Cloud, minimized context, and advisory Claude Haiku 5.5 findings.

Beta 0.1.0-beta.1Published with ad-hoc signatures; not notarized. TraceRook Cloud and Claude Code review have passed together. Codex remains unverified. Download and setup.

Why Claude is in the pipeline

Local deterministic policy handles concrete catastrophic evidence. TraceRook Cloud uses Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5 for bounded contextual findings and can recommend an exact-action human review. The model cannot grant permissions or erase a deterministic critical denial.

The signed native app and service, production Cloud API, genuine Haiku response, and actual Claude Code 2.1.290 Bash callback have passed together. The requested review was resolved through native Allow once; the harmless sentinel executed afterward. A separate deterministic critical canary was denied and its sentinel remained absent. This is evidence for the tested path, not universal agent coverage. Codex remains unverified.

TraceRook operates the Cloud connection

The background service sends authorized requests to https://api.tracerook.dev. The Cloud backend calls Anthropic's first-party Messages API using TraceRook's company-owned key. The Mac never needs that key.

In Settings → AI Provider → TraceRook Cloud, enter the access code provided with your invitation and accept the displayed consent. Device credentials stay only in service session memory. Re-enter access after the service restarts; no Keychain access occurs. Direct Anthropic BYOK is unavailable in this beta.

Enrollment, operator availability, the local analysis switch, and a validated response are separate states. Use the explicit pause/resume controls. The static website has no credential form and sends no provider requests. Read beta requirements and setup.

What reaches Claude

  • A coarse task category.
  • A coarse action category.
  • Enumerated local signal codes.

The current conservative projection excludes raw commands, paths, code, file contents, transcripts, and arbitrary summary prose. A separate secret/path/URL/entropy preflight checks the projection before transmission. Local exact-action previews remain on the Mac. Less context limits what the model can infer; broader real-case evaluation remains in progress.

Claude does not grant permissions

Responses use a strict versioned schema and must match request identity, model, provenance, timestamps, and bounds. Malformed or late results cannot authorize an action. A model-only critical finding is routed to human review; concrete local critical evidence retains precedence.

A pending review binds the exact session, event, tool call, action fingerprint, and invocation nonce. Allow once clears only TraceRook's gate for that invocation. Native agent permissions still apply. The native review displays the matching service-redacted action preview; a missing preview disables Allow once.

Bounded deadlines and actual evidence

Hook and provider deadlines are bounded, and human review expires after at most 45 seconds. The manual Claude setup gives the synchronous host hook an 85-second timeout; a shorter host deadline can end the callback before the human review finishes. Skipped or host-timed-out hooks may permit execution.

A genuine native Cloud receipt reported Haiku 5.5, 929 input tokens, 232 output tokens, and 2.751 seconds. That is one measured request, not a latency guarantee. Current checks pass 81 local tests, 60 Worker tests, and 24 native appearance cases. The broader hosted evaluation corpus and clean tester installation remain in progress.

No customer software inference allotment or company spending cutoff is enabled. Abuse controls, bounded requests, concurrency limits, revocation, platform limits, and the operator disable switch remain. Payment collection and subscriptions are not implemented.

Consent and retention

Explicit versioned consent explains the transmitted categories and that TraceRook sends them onward to Anthropic. Context can remain sensitive even without raw source. Anthropic retention follows its API terms.

Cloud analysis receipts are retained for 30 days, account/device metadata until deletion, usage aggregates for 90 days, and temporary verdict cache for up to 10 minutes. Platform outages can delay physical cache cleanup; expired cache entries are not served. Local history and Cloud account deletion are separate controls. A failed deletion does not establish server-side deletion.

Cloud Demo and the Local API Demo remain synthetic; their findings never count as genuine provider evidence. See the current release scope and coverage limits.

Based on the MVP1 specification, the additive MVP2 specification, and the acceptance matrix · October 8, 2026.
